purpose: Assesses whether the organization creates and keeps up to date technical documentation for its high-risk AI system, demonstrating compliance with the Act's requirements before the system is placed on the market or put into service.
summary: Article 11 requires providers to draw up technical documentation before a high-risk AI system is placed on the market or put into service, and to keep it up to date. The documentation must be drafted in a way that demonstrates the system complies with Chapter III Section 2 requirements and must contain, at minimum, the elements set out in Annex IV (general description, design specifications, development process, monitoring/functioning/control capabilities, risk management measures, and more).
expectedStatementElements: Whether technical documentation exists for the system, covering the Annex IV elements, before market placement or service
How technical documentation is kept up to date as the system changes post-deployment
How the documentation demonstrates compliance with the specific Chapter III Section 2 requirements (Articles 9-15)
What review or approval process governs technical documentation before it's considered complete
evidenceExamples: Technical documentation package covering Annex IV elements (system description, design specs, development process, monitoring capabilities, risk management)
Version history showing technical documentation updates aligned with system changes
Cross-reference mapping technical documentation sections to specific Chapter III Section 2 requirements
Documentation review/approval records prior to market placement or service deployment
commonGaps: Technical documentation is created after the system is already in production, rather than before deployment
Documentation isn't updated when the system changes, so it no longer accurately reflects what's actually running
Documentation doesn't clearly map back to the specific Article 9-15 requirements it's meant to demonstrate compliance with
interviewQuestions: Was our technical documentation finished before this system went live, or is it being written after the fact?
When the system changes, does someone actually go back and update the documentation?
If a regulator asked how our documentation proves compliance with Articles 9 through 15, could we show them directly?
Who reviews and signs off on technical documentation before it's considered complete?
